title: Maharashtra Bars Quota Candidates From Open Category Seats in Major Reservation Overhaul

body:
The Maharashtra government has tightened its reservation framework with a significant policy change that bars candidates who secured admission through quota or relaxed eligibility criteria from competing for open-category seats. The move aims to protect the merit pool in the general category from being diluted by candidates who benefit from both reservation and open-category pathways.

The decision addresses a long-standing grievance among open-category aspirants who argued that quota beneficiaries effectively occupied seats meant for unreserved candidates when they scored high enough to qualify in the general pool. Under the new rules, candidates who avail themselves of any reservation benefit—whether caste-based, economically weaker section (EWS), or other relaxations—will be locked into their respective quota categories for that admission cycle.

For NRIs with roots in Maharashtra, the change could reshape how their children navigate the state's competitive entrance landscape, particularly for professional courses in medicine and engineering. Education consultants say the policy brings Maharashtra in line with a stricter interpretation that several other states have debated but not yet implemented.

The ruling is expected to face legal challenges, as previous attempts to restrict cross-category mobility have drawn constitutional scrutiny. Student organisations have offered a mixed response—reserved-category groups call it discriminatory, while open-category advocates see it as a necessary correction.
author: Diaspora Desk
